title: Length of a Loop in a Linked List
statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked list that may contain a loop: the `next` pointer of the last node may point back to some earlier node (or to itself) instead of being null.

Return the **length of the loop**, that is, the number of distinct nodes that lie on the cycle. If the list has no loop, return `0`.

Node values are irrelevant and may repeat, so two different nodes can hold the same value. Nodes are identified by their position in the list, not by their value.

In the input the list is described by its values in order, plus the index of the node that the last node's `next` points to (`-1` if the list ends normally).
input_format:
The first line contains `n`, the number of nodes.
The second line contains `n` integers: the node values from head to tail.
The third line contains an integer `idx`: the 0-indexed position of the node that the tail points to, or `-1` if there is no loop.
output_format: Print a single integer: the number of nodes in the loop, or `0` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The tail (50) points back to the node at index 2 (30), so the loop is 30 -> 40 -> 50 -> 30 and contains 3 nodes.
The tail points to nothing, so there is no loop even though all values are equal.
The tail points to itself, so the loop has a single node. The values being equal do not matter; the loop is made of nodes, not values.

hints: First decide whether there is a loop at all. Two pointers moving at different speeds will meet inside the loop if and only if one exists.
Once the slow and fast pointers meet, both are standing on a node of the cycle.
Keep one pointer fixed on that node and move the other one step by step until they meet again, counting the steps. That count is the loop length.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    idx = int(data[1 + n])
    nxt = [i + 1 for i in range(n)]
    nxt[n - 1] = idx
    slow = fast = 0
    while fast != -1 and nxt[fast] != -1:
        slow = nxt[slow]
        fast = nxt[nxt[fast]]
        if slow == fast:
            cnt = 1
            cur = nxt[slow]
            while cur != slow:
                cur = nxt[cur]
                cnt += 1
            print(cnt)
            return
    print(0)

main()
brute:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
idx = int(data[1 + n])
seen = {}
cur = 0
step = 0
ans = 0
while cur != -1:
    if cur in seen:
        ans = step - seen[cur]
        break
    seen[cur] = step
    step += 1
    cur = cur + 1 if cur < n - 1 else idx
print(ans)
